debug.description:
Options for `@docusaurus/plugin-debug`. Use `false` to disable, or `true`
to enable even in production.

onInlineTags.description: The behavior of Docusaurus when it finds inline tags.

routeBasePath.description:
URL route for the docs section of your site. **DO NOT** include a
trailing slash. Use `/` for shipping docs without base path.

editUrl.description:
Base URL to edit your site. The final URL is computed by `editUrl +
relativeDocPath`. Using a function allows more nuanced control for each
file. Omitting this variable entirely will disable edit links.

editCurrentVersion.description:
The edit URL will always target the current version doc instead of older
versions. Ignored when `editUrl` is a function.

editLocalizedFiles.description:
The edit URL will target the localized file, instead of the original
unlocalized file. Ignored when `editUrl` is a function.

showLastUpdateTime.description: Whether to display the last date the doc was updated.

showLastUpdateAuthor.description: Whether to display the author who last updated the doc.

numberPrefixParser.description:
Custom parsing logic to extract number prefixes from file names. Use
`false` to disable this behavior and leave the docs untouched, and
`true` to use the default parser.

breadcrumbs.description: Enable or disable the breadcrumbs on doc pages.

path.description:
Path to the docs content directory on the file system, relative to site
directory.

sidebarPath.description:
Path to sidebar configuration. Use `false` to disable sidebars, or
`undefined` to create a fully autogenerated sidebar.

lastVersion.description:
The version navigated to in priority and displayed by default for docs
navbar items.

onlyIncludeVersions.description: Only include a subset of all available versions.

disableVersioning.description:
Explicitly disable versioning even when multiple versions exist. This
will make the site only include the current version. Will error if
`includeCurrentVersion: false` and `disableVersioning: true`.

includeCurrentVersion.description: Include the current version of your docs.

path.description:
The base path of the version, will be appended to `baseUrl` +
`routeBasePath`.

label.description: The label of the version to be used in badges, dropdowns, etc.

banner.description: The banner to show at the top of a doc of that version.

badge.description: Show a badge with the version label at the top of each doc.

noIndex.description: Prevents search engines from indexing this version

className.description: Add a custom class name to the <html> element of each doc.

versions.description: Independent customization of each version's properties.

sidebarCollapsible.description: Whether sidebar categories are collapsible by default.

sidebarCollapsed.description: Whether sidebar categories are collapsed by default.

include.description:
Array of glob patterns matching Markdown files to be built, relative to
the content path.

exclude.description:
Array of glob patterns matching Markdown files to be excluded. Serves
as refinement based on the `include` option.

docsRootComponent.description:
Parent component of all the docs plugin pages (including all versions).
Stays mounted when navigation between docs pages and versions.

docVersionRootComponent.description:
Parent component of all docs pages of an individual version:
- docs pages with sidebars
- tags pages
Stays mounted when navigation between pages of that specific version.

docRootComponent.description:
Parent component of all docs pages with sidebars:
- regular docs pages
- category generated index pages
Stays mounted when navigation between such pages.

docItemComponent.description: Main doc container, with TOC, pagination, etc.

docTagDocListComponent.description: Root component of the "docs containing tag X" page.

docTagsListComponent.description: Root component of the tags list page

docCategoryGeneratedIndexComponent.description: Root component of the generated category index page.

tagsBasePath.description:
URL route for the tags section of your doc version. Will be appended to
`routeBasePath`. **DO NOT** include a trailing slash.

onInlineTags.description: The behavior of Docusaurus when it finds inline tags.

routeBasePath.description:
URL route for the blog section of your site. **DO NOT** include a
trailing slash. Use `/` to put the blog at root path.

editUrl.description:
Base URL to edit your site. The final URL is computed by `editUrl +
relativePostPath`. Using a function allows more nuanced control for each
file. Omitting this variable entirely will disable edit links.

editLocalizedFiles.description:
The edit URL will target the localized file, instead of the original
unlocalized file. Ignored when `editUrl` is a function.

showLastUpdateTime.description: Whether to display the last date the blog post was updated.

showLastUpdateAuthor.description: Whether to display the author who last updated the blog post.

path.description:
Path to the blog content directory on the file system, relative to site
directory.

include.description:
Array of glob patterns matching Markdown files to be built, relative to
the content path.

exclude.description:
Array of glob patterns matching Markdown files to be excluded. Serves as
refinement based on the `include` option.

tagsBasePath.description:
URL route for the tags section of your blog. Will be appended to
`routeBasePath`.

pageBasePath.description:
URL route for the pages section of your blog. Will be appended to
`routeBasePath`.

archiveBasePath.description:
URL route for the archive section of your blog. Will be appended to
`routeBasePath`. **DO NOT** include a trailing slash. Use `null` to
disable generation of archive.

postsPerPage.description:
Number of posts to show per page in the listing page. Use `'ALL'` to
display all posts on one listing page.

blogListComponent.description: Root component of the blog listing page.

blogPostComponent.description: Root component of each blog post page.

blogTagsListComponent.description: Root component of the tags list page.

blogTagsPostsComponent.description: Root component of the "posts containing tag" page.

blogAuthorsListComponent.description: Root component of the authors list page.

blogAuthorsPostsComponent.description: Root component of the "posts containing author" page.

blogArchiveComponent.description: Root component of the blog archive page.

blogTitle.description: Blog page title for better SEO.

blogDescription.description: Blog page meta description for better SEO.

blogSidebarCount.description:
Number of blog post elements to show in the blog sidebar. `'ALL'` to show
all blog posts; `0` to disable.

truncateMarker.description: Truncate marker marking where the summary ends.

showReadingTime.description: Show estimated reading time for the blog post.

xslt.description: User-provided XSLT config for feeds, un-normalized

type.description: Type of feed to be generated. Use `null` to disable generation.

copyright.description: Copyright notice. Required because the feed library marked it that.

createFeedItems.description: Allow control over the construction of BlogFeedItems

limit.description: Limits the feed to the specified number of posts, false|null for all

authorsMapPath.description: Path to the authors map file, relative to the blog content directory.

readingTime.description: A callback to customize the reading time number displayed.

sortPosts.description: Governs the direction of blog post sorting.

processBlogPosts.description:
An optional function which can be used to transform blog posts
(filter, modify, delete, etc...).

onInlineAuthors.description: The behavior of Docusaurus when it finds inline authors.

onUntruncatedBlogPosts.description: The behavior of Docusaurus when it finds untruncated blog posts.

filename.description:
The path to the created sitemap file, relative to the output directory.
Useful if you have two plugin instances outputting two files.

ignorePatterns.description:
A list of glob patterns; matching route paths will be filtered from the
sitemap. Note that you may need to include the base URL in here.

lastmod.description:
Defines the format of the "lastmod" sitemap item entry, between:
- null: do not compute/add a "lastmod" sitemap entry
- "date": add a "lastmod" sitemap entry without time (YYYY-MM-DD)
- "datetime": add a "lastmod" sitemap entry with time (ISO 8601 datetime)

Options for `@docusaurus/plugin-google-analytics`. Only enabled when the
key is present.

gtag.description:
Options for `@docusaurus/plugin-google-gtag`. Only enabled when the key

timeout.description: Default timeout for async expect matchers in milliseconds, defaults to 5000ms.

threshold.description:
an acceptable perceived color difference between the same pixel in compared images, ranging from `0` (strict) and
`1` (lax). `"pixelmatch"` comparator computes color difference in
[YIQ color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YIQ) and defaults `threshold` value to `0.2`.

maxDiffPixels.description:
an acceptable amount of pixels that could be different, unset by default. Note that `threshold` defines which
pixels are considered different.

maxDiffPixelRatio.description:
an acceptable ratio of pixels that are different to the total amount of pixels, between `0` and `1` , unset by
default. Note that `threshold` defines which pixels are considered different.

type.description:
Format of the screenshots taken when the snapshot name is omitted, defaults to `"png"`. Snapshots with an explicit
name use the format matching their `.png` or `.webp` extension.

pathTemplate.description:
A template controlling location of the screenshots. See
[testProject.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-snapshot-path-template)
for details.

timeout.description:
Default timeout for
[expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(name[, options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions#page-assertions-to-have-screenshot-1)
in milliseconds, defaults to the global expect timeout. Setting to `0` disables the timeout.

pathTemplate.description:
A template controlling location of the aria snapshots. See
[testProject.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-snapshot-path-template)
for details.

children.description:
Controls how children of the snapshot root are matched against the actual accessibility tree. This is equivalent to
adding a `/children` property at the top of every aria snapshot template. Individual snapshots can override this by
including an explicit `/children` property.

threshold.description:
an acceptable perceived color difference between the same pixel in compared images, ranging from `0` (strict) and
`1` (lax). `"pixelmatch"` comparator computes color difference in
[YIQ color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YIQ) and defaults `threshold` value to `0.2`.

maxDiffPixels.description:
an acceptable amount of pixels that could be different, unset by default. Note that `threshold` defines which
pixels are considered different.

maxDiffPixelRatio.description:
an acceptable ratio of pixels that are different to the total amount of pixels, between `0` and `1` , unset by
default. Note that `threshold` defines which pixels are considered different.

timeout.description: timeout for toPass method in milliseconds.

intervals.description: probe intervals for toPass method in milliseconds.

expect.description:
Configuration for the `expect` assertion library.

Use [testConfig.expect](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-expect) to change this option
for all projects.

fullyParallel.description:
Playwright Test runs tests in parallel. In order to achieve that, it runs several worker processes that run at the
same time. By default, **test files** are run in parallel. Tests in a single file are run in order, in the same
worker process.

You can configure entire test project to concurrently run all tests in all files using this option.

grep.description:
Filter to only run tests with a title matching one of the patterns. For example, passing `grep: /cart/` should only
run tests with "cart" in the title. Also available globally and in the [command line](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli) with the `-g`
option. The regular expression will be tested against the string that consists of the project name, the test file
name, the `test.describe` name (if any), the test name and the test tags divided by spaces, e.g. `chromium
my-test.spec.ts my-suite my-test`.

`grep` option is also useful for [tagging tests](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-annotations#tag-tests).

grepInvert.description:
Filter to only run tests with a title **not** matching any of the patterns. This is the opposite of
[testProject.grep](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-grep). Also available globally
and in the [command line](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli) with the `--grep-invert` option.

`grepInvert` option is also useful for [tagging tests](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-annotations#tag-tests).

metadata.description: Metadata that will be put directly to the test report serialized as JSON.

name.description:
Project name is visible in the report and during test execution.

**NOTE** Playwright executes the configuration file multiple times. Do not dynamically produce non-stable values in
your configuration.

repeatEach.description:
The number of times to repeat each test, useful for debugging flaky tests.

Use [testConfig.repeatEach](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-repeat-each) to change
this option for all projects.

respectGitIgnore.description:
Whether to skip entries from `.gitignore` when searching for test files. By default, if neither
[testConfig.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-dir) nor
[testProject.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-test-dir) are explicitly
specified, Playwright will ignore any test files matching `.gitignore` entries. This option allows to override that
behavior.

retries.description:
The maximum number of retry attempts given to failed tests. Learn more about
[test retries](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-retries#retries).

Use [test.describe.configure([options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-describe-configure) to
change the number of retries for a specific file or a group of tests.

Use [testConfig.retries](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-retries) to change this
option for all projects.

snapshotDir.description:
The base directory, relative to the config file, for snapshot files created with `toMatchSnapshot`. Defaults to
[testProject.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-test-dir).

The directory for each test can be accessed by
[testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir) and
[testInfo.snapshotPath(...name[, options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-path).

This path will serve as the base directory for each test file snapshot directory. Setting `snapshotDir` to
`'snapshots'`, the [testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir)
would resolve to `snapshots/a.spec.js-snapshots`.

testIgnore.description:
Files matching one of these patterns are not executed as test files. Matching is performed against the absolute
file path. Strings are treated as glob patterns.

For example, `'**\/test-assets/**'` will ignore any files in the `test-assets` directory.

Use [testConfig.testIgnore](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-ignore) to change
this option for all projects.

testMatch.description:
Only the files matching one of these patterns are executed as test files. Matching is performed against the
absolute file path. Strings are treated as glob patterns.

By default, Playwright looks for files matching the following glob pattern: `**\/*.@(spec|test).?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)`.
This means JavaScript or TypeScript files with `".test"` or `".spec"` suffix, for example
`login-screen.wrong-credentials.spec.ts`.

Use [testConfig.testMatch](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-match) to change this
option for all projects.

timeout.description:
Timeout for each test in milliseconds. Defaults to 30 seconds.

This is a base timeout for all tests. Each test can configure its own timeout with
[test.setTimeout(timeout)](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-set-timeout). Each file or a group of
tests can configure the timeout with
[test.describe.configure([options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-describe-configure).

Use [testConfig.timeout](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-timeout) to change this
option for all projects.

command.description: Shell command to start. For example `npm run start`..

cwd.description: Current working directory of the spawned process, defaults to the directory of the configuration file.

env.description: Environment variables to set for the command, `process.env` by default.

gracefulShutdown.description:
How to shut down the process. If unspecified, the process group is forcefully `SIGKILL`ed. If set to `{ signal:
'SIGTERM', timeout: 500 }`, the process group is sent a `SIGTERM` signal, followed by `SIGKILL` if it doesn't exit
within 500ms. You can also use `SIGINT` as the signal instead. A `0` timeout means no `SIGKILL` will be sent.
Windows doesn't support `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` signals, so this option is ignored on Windows. Note that shutting
down a Docker container requires `SIGTERM`.

ignoreHTTPSErrors.description: Whether to ignore HTTPS errors when fetching the `url`. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: Specifies a custom name for the web server. This name will be prefixed to log messages. Defaults to `[WebServer]`.

port.description:
The port that your http server is expected to appear on. It does wait until it accepts connections. Either `port`
or `url` should be specified.

reuseExistingServer.description:
If true, it will re-use an existing server on the `port` or `url` when available. If no server is running on that
`port` or `url`, it will run the command to start a new server. If `false`, it will throw if an existing process is
listening on the `port` or `url`. This should be commonly set to `!process.env.CI` to allow the local dev server
when running tests locally.

stderr.description: Whether to pipe the stderr of the command to the process stderr or ignore it. Defaults to `"pipe"`.

stdout.description:
If `"pipe"`, it will pipe the stdout of the command to the process stdout. If `"ignore"`, it will ignore the stdout
of the command. Default to `"ignore"`.

Regular expression to wait for in the `stdout` of the command output. Named capture groups are stored in the
environment, for example `/Listening on port (?<my_server_port>\d+)/` will store the port number in
`process.env['MY_SERVER_PORT']`.

stderr.description:
Regular expression to wait for in the `stderr` of the command output. Named capture groups are stored in the
environment, for example `/Listening on port (?<my_server_port>\d+)/` will store the port number in
`process.env['MY_SERVER_PORT']`.

wait.description: Consider command started only when given output has been produced.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the process to start up and be available in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000.

url.description:
The url on your http server that is expected to return a 2xx, 3xx, 400, 401, 402, or 403 status code when the
server is ready to accept connections. Redirects (3xx status codes) are being followed and the new location is
checked. Either `port` or `url` should be specified.

command.description: Shell command to start. For example `npm run start`..

cwd.description: Current working directory of the spawned process, defaults to the directory of the configuration file.

env.description: Environment variables to set for the command, `process.env` by default.

gracefulShutdown.description:
How to shut down the process. If unspecified, the process group is forcefully `SIGKILL`ed. If set to `{ signal:
'SIGTERM', timeout: 500 }`, the process group is sent a `SIGTERM` signal, followed by `SIGKILL` if it doesn't exit
within 500ms. You can also use `SIGINT` as the signal instead. A `0` timeout means no `SIGKILL` will be sent.
Windows doesn't support `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` signals, so this option is ignored on Windows. Note that shutting
down a Docker container requires `SIGTERM`.

ignoreHTTPSErrors.description: Whether to ignore HTTPS errors when fetching the `url`. Defaults to `false`.

name.description: Specifies a custom name for the web server. This name will be prefixed to log messages. Defaults to `[WebServer]`.

port.description:
The port that your http server is expected to appear on. It does wait until it accepts connections. Either `port`
or `url` should be specified.

reuseExistingServer.description:
If true, it will re-use an existing server on the `port` or `url` when available. If no server is running on that
`port` or `url`, it will run the command to start a new server. If `false`, it will throw if an existing process is
listening on the `port` or `url`. This should be commonly set to `!process.env.CI` to allow the local dev server
when running tests locally.

stderr.description: Whether to pipe the stderr of the command to the process stderr or ignore it. Defaults to `"pipe"`.

stdout.description:
If `"pipe"`, it will pipe the stdout of the command to the process stdout. If `"ignore"`, it will ignore the stdout
of the command. Default to `"ignore"`.

Regular expression to wait for in the `stdout` of the command output. Named capture groups are stored in the
environment, for example `/Listening on port (?<my_server_port>\d+)/` will store the port number in
`process.env['MY_SERVER_PORT']`.

stderr.description:
Regular expression to wait for in the `stderr` of the command output. Named capture groups are stored in the
environment, for example `/Listening on port (?<my_server_port>\d+)/` will store the port number in
`process.env['MY_SERVER_PORT']`.

wait.description: Consider command started only when given output has been produced.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the process to start up and be available in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000.

url.description:
The url on your http server that is expected to return a 2xx, 3xx, 400, 401, 402, or 403 status code when the
server is ready to accept connections. Redirects (3xx status codes) are being followed and the new location is
checked. Either `port` or `url` should be specified.

external.description:
Paths to exclude from the transpilation expressed as a list of glob patterns. Typically heavy JS bundles that your
test uses are listed here.

commit.description: Whether to capture commit and pull request information such as hash, author, timestamp.

timeout.description: Default timeout for async expect matchers in milliseconds, defaults to 5000ms.

maxDiffPixels.description:
An acceptable amount of pixels that could be different, unset by default. Note that `threshold` defines which
pixels are considered different.

maxDiffPixelRatio.description:
An acceptable ratio of pixels that are different to the total amount of pixels, between `0` and `1` , unset by
default. Note that `threshold` defines which pixels are considered different.

threshold.description:
An acceptable perceived color difference between the same pixel in compared images, ranging from `0` (strict) and
`1` (lax). `"pixelmatch"` comparator computes color difference in
[YIQ color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YIQ) and defaults `threshold` value to `0.2`.

type.description:
Format of the screenshots taken when the snapshot name is omitted, defaults to `"png"`. Snapshots with an explicit
name use the format matching their `.png` or `.webp` extension.

pathTemplate.description:
A template controlling location of the screenshots. See
[testConfig.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-snapshot-path-template)
for details.

A template controlling location of the aria snapshots. See
[testConfig.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-snapshot-path-template)
for details.

children.description:
Controls how children of the snapshot root are matched against the actual accessibility tree. This is equivalent to
adding a `/children` property at the top of every aria snapshot template. Individual snapshots can override this by
including an explicit `/children` property.

maxDiffPixels.description:
An acceptable amount of pixels that could be different, unset by default. Note that `threshold` defines which
pixels are considered different.

maxDiffPixelRatio.description:
An acceptable ratio of pixels that are different to the total amount of pixels, between `0` and `1` , unset by
default. Note that `threshold` defines which pixels are considered different.

threshold.description:
An acceptable perceived color difference between the same pixel in compared images, ranging from `0` (strict) and
`1` (lax). `"pixelmatch"` comparator computes color difference in
[YIQ color space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YIQ) and defaults `threshold` value to `0.2`.

intervals.description: Probe intervals for toPass method in milliseconds.

timeout.description: Timeout for toPass method in milliseconds.

max.description: The maximum number of slow test files to report. Defaults to `5`.

threshold.description: Test file duration in milliseconds that is considered slow. Defaults to 5 minutes.

respectGitIgnore.description:
Whether to skip entries from `.gitignore` when searching for test files. By default, if neither
[testConfig.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-dir) nor
[testProject.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testproject#test-project-test-dir) are explicitly
specified, Playwright will ignore any test files matching `.gitignore` entries.

current.description: The index of the shard to execute, one-based.

snapshotDir.description:
**NOTE** Use
[testConfig.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-snapshot-path-template)
to configure snapshot paths.

The base directory, relative to the config file, for snapshot files created with `toMatchSnapshot`. Defaults to
[testConfig.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-dir).

**Usage**

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  snapshotDir: './snapshots',
});
```

**Details**

The directory for each test can be accessed by
[testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir) and
[testInfo.snapshotPath(...name[, options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-path).

This path will serve as the base directory for each test file snapshot directory. Setting `snapshotDir` to
`'snapshots'`, the [testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir)
would resolve to `snapshots/a.spec.js-snapshots`.

updateSnapshots.description:
Whether to update expected snapshots with the actual results produced by the test run. Defaults to `'default'`.
- `'all'` - All tests that are executed will update snapshots.
- `'changed'` - All tests that are executed will update snapshots that did not match. Matching snapshots will not
  be updated. Also creates missing snapshots.
- `'missing'` - Missing snapshots are created, for example when authoring a new test and running it for the first
  time. Tests that only create missing snapshots pass.
- `'none'` - No snapshots are updated.
- `'default'` - Missing snapshots are created, but the tests that create them fail, so that the run does not
  silently pass in CI. This is the default.

Learn more about [snapshots](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots).

**Usage**

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  updateSnapshots: 'default',
});
```

updateSourceMethod.description:
Defines how to update snapshots in the source code.
- `'patch'` - Create a unified diff file that can be used to update the source code later. This is the default.
- `'3way'` - Generate merge conflict markers in source code. This allows user to manually pick relevant changes,
  as if they are resolving a merge conflict in the IDE.
- `'overwrite'` - Overwrite the source code with the new snapshot values.

entries.description:
How to shut down the process. If unspecified, the process group is forcefully `SIGKILL`ed. If set to `{ signal:
'SIGTERM', timeout: 500 }`, the process group is sent a `SIGTERM` signal, followed by `SIGKILL` if it doesn't exit
within 500ms. You can also use `SIGINT` as the signal instead. A `0` timeout means no `SIGKILL` will be sent.
Windows doesn't support `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` signals, so this option is ignored on Windows. Note that shutting
down a Docker container requires `SIGTERM`.

entries.description:
How to shut down the process. If unspecified, the process group is forcefully `SIGKILL`ed. If set to `{ signal:
'SIGTERM', timeout: 500 }`, the process group is sent a `SIGTERM` signal, followed by `SIGKILL` if it doesn't exit
within 500ms. You can also use `SIGINT` as the signal instead. A `0` timeout means no `SIGKILL` will be sent.
Windows doesn't support `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` signals, so this option is ignored on Windows. Note that shutting
down a Docker container requires `SIGTERM`.

entries.description:
**NOTE** Use
[testConfig.snapshotPathTemplate](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-snapshot-path-template)
to configure snapshot paths.

The base directory, relative to the config file, for snapshot files created with `toMatchSnapshot`. Defaults to
[testConfig.testDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testconfig#test-config-test-dir).

**Usage**

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  snapshotDir: './snapshots',
});
```

**Details**

The directory for each test can be accessed by
[testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir) and
[testInfo.snapshotPath(...name[, options])](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-path).

This path will serve as the base directory for each test file snapshot directory. Setting `snapshotDir` to
`'snapshots'`, the [testInfo.snapshotDir](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo#test-info-snapshot-dir)
would resolve to `snapshots/a.spec.js-snapshots`.

entries.description:
Whether to update expected snapshots with the actual results produced by the test run. Defaults to `'default'`.
- `'all'` - All tests that are executed will update snapshots.
- `'changed'` - All tests that are executed will update snapshots that did not match. Matching snapshots will not
  be updated. Also creates missing snapshots.
- `'missing'` - Missing snapshots are created, for example when authoring a new test and running it for the first
  time. Tests that only create missing snapshots pass.
- `'none'` - No snapshots are updated.
- `'default'` - Missing snapshots are created, but the tests that create them fail, so that the run does not
  silently pass in CI. This is the default.

Learn more about [snapshots](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots).

**Usage**

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  updateSnapshots: 'default',
});
```

entries.description:
Defines how to update snapshots in the source code.
- `'patch'` - Create a unified diff file that can be used to update the source code later. This is the default.
- `'3way'` - Generate merge conflict markers in source code. This allows user to manually pick relevant changes,
  as if they are resolving a merge conflict in the IDE.
- `'overwrite'` - Overwrite the source code with the new snapshot values.
